discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 16262e09e. I kept `releaseQualityClone` scoped to responses that are still forwarded and added `releaseRejectedQualityResponse` only at the pinned, priority, and round-robin branches that actually discard an invalid response. It cancels both the quality clone and the original tee branch, allowing the shared upstream source to receive cancellation. The new regression test uses a never-ending primary SSE source, verifies fallback remains readable, and asserts that the discarded primary receives `cancel()`. I intentionally did not apply this generically to `runtimeUnits`, because that path can still return its `lastResponse`.

Good catch, fixed in 0a7be331a. The helper now takes a `decrementPendingRequest` flag (default true). Transform-time call sites keep the decrement; the three flush-time call sites pass `false` because `flush()` already does the unconditional `trackPendingRequest(..., false)` at entry, so the counter is no longer decremented twice.

Quick correction on the no-op claim: `disconnect()` on LocalDatastore does call `clearInterval(this.heartbeat)` (`node_modules/bottleneck/lib/LocalDatastore.js` line 74), which is what we want here — it clears the reservoir refresh timer without entering the "stopped" state. That said, you are right that `stop({ dropWaitingJobs: true })` is the cleaner test-only shutdown signal and would also settle the `yieldLoop`. I left `disconnect()` in this iteration to keep the test reset symmetric with the runtime eviction paths, but happy to switch to `stop({ dropWaitingJobs: true })` here specifically (since this helper is test-only — no in-flight job poisoning concern) if you prefer.

Good catch — fixed.

The auto-enable branch in `reconcileEnabledConnections` was instantiating `new Bottleneck(...)` directly, so the `executing` listener that updates `lastDispatchAt` never got registered. Combined with `lastDispatchAt.get(key) ?? 0`, the watchdog computed `stalledMs ≈ now - 0` ≈ Unix time and false-triggered on the first reservoir-refresh wait — exactly as you described.

Two-part fix:

1. Reconcile path now goes through `getLimiter(provider, connectionId)` instead of constructing directly, so the `queued`/`executing` listeners and `lastDispatchAt` heartbeat are wired up the same way as on-demand creation.
2. Watchdog hardened: if `lastDispatchAt` is `undefined` for any reason, seed it on the current tick and skip — never compute stall against a missing baseline.

Pushed as a follow-up commit on this branch.

Applied in 0f95330. Wrapped the stream body with a TransformStream so the semaphore slot is released in the `flush` callback when the stream is fully consumed, rather than in a try/finally that fired on header reception.

Fixed — now imports `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` from config/constants and applies it via `AbortSignal.timeout()` + `mergeAbortSignals()`, matching the BaseExecutor pattern exactly. No more hanging connections.
